main_text.l: uitatumque omnium ac rerum publicarum rationem praeceptaque tradit, ac propterea πολιτικὰ[?] appellatur. Quarum omnium origo mens hominis ea est, quae πρακτικὴ[?] dicitur, & alicuius rei agedæ gratia ratiocinatur. At vero ea, alte-ra, cuius actio contemplatio est, proficiscitur alterū philosophiæ genus, quod θεωρητικὸν[?] nominant. Hoc autem multiplex esse dicitur: quandoquidem genera eorū quæ sunt, in quibus versatur, va-ria sunt. Quædam enim re ipsa, & ratione à sensibili materia seiuncta sunt ac separata: in quo genere primæ substantiæ consistunt, quæ diuinæ subiiciuntur philosophiæ, propterea quod immutabiles sint, & insensibiles ac æternæ. Etenim alias esse substantias primas immuta-biles,

page.notes: The Greek words (πολιτικὰ, πρακτικὴ, θεωρητικὸν) are read from a small, slightly blurred print and are marked [?]. "agedæ" is printed as such (probably for agendæ). The word "alterū" is a printing reading; the line ends "alte-ra" and "gra-tia" are hyphenated as printed. The text ends mid-sentence with "immuta-biles," and continues on the next page.
